title: SDK Contract Testing and Sample Workflows
body:
> **Archived 2025-11-02:** this page is superseded by "SDK Contract Testing and Sample Workflows" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

This page describes how we write SDK contract tests, wire up CI workflows, and structure sample test suites for the Redwood Inference SDKs. It is aimed at SDK authors, integration engineers, and platform CI owners. The intent is to keep language bindings and client libraries compatible with the Redwood API surface from release to release, and to give engineers templates they can copy straight into their projects.

When to use SDK contract tests

- Ahead of any public SDK release or patch that alters request/response shapes.
- Before a runtime or major API change ships (model routing, function calling schema changes).
- As part of nightly CI for long-lived SDK repositories.

Test types and scope

1) Contract unit tests (fast, deterministic)
   - Check that request builders encode parameters into the expected HTTP payloads.
   - Check that response parsers tolerate optional or missing fields.
   - Run against a stubbed HTTP server or request fixtures.

2) Integration contract tests (CI gated)
   - Call a sandbox Redwood API or test harness endpoint.
   - Cover end-to-end serialization, headers, auth refresh, and streaming/chunked responses.

3) Regression scenario tests
   - Small prompt sets with expected token patterns to catch behavior regressions (not full evals).

Ownership and SLOs

- SDK Team (owner): owns the test suites and CI pipelines.
- DevEx Platform (support): supplies the sandbox endpoint, test tokens, and shared GitHub Actions templates.
- SLO: PR test runs must finish within a CI max time of 20 minutes; nightly runs may take up to 1 hour.

Contract schema (recommended minimal surface)

Keep a small, explicit contract YAML at tests/contract.yaml in the repo root. Unit and integration tests both treat it as the canonical expected shape. Example:

```yaml
api_contract_version: 1
endpoints:
  - name: text_generate
    method: POST
    path: /v1/generate
    required_request_fields:
      - model
      - input
    optional_request_fields:
      - max_tokens
      - temperature
    response_expectations:
      - field: output.choices
        type: list

  - name: embeddings
    method: POST
    path: /v1/embeddings
    required_request_fields:
      - model
      - input
    response_expectations:
      - field: embeddings
        type: list
        item_type: float
```

Sample workflows

A. PR fast-path: unit contract tests only (best for contributor experience)

1. On PR: lint, unit contract tests, and quick type checks.
2. Once unit contract tests pass, a maintainer can approve the merge to main.
3. On merge: the full integration pipeline runs (see B).

B. Merge gate: full integration + nightly regression

1. On push to main: build SDK artifacts and run integration contract tests against the sandbox.
2. On integration failure, an issue is opened automatically with artifacts and the last failing request/response.
3. Nightly: the extended regression suite runs across the language matrix below.

CI template (GitHub Actions example)

```yaml
name: SDK Contract CI
on: [pull_request, push]
jobs:
  contract_unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup runtime
        run: ./ci/setup-env.sh
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: ci/install_deps.sh
      - name: Run contract unit tests
        run: ci/run_contract_unit_tests.sh
  integration_tests:
    needs: contract_unit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run integration contract tests
        env:
          REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN }}
        run: ci/run_integration_tests.sh
```

Testing matrix (example)

| SDK language | Unit coverage | Integration frequency | Responsible owner |
|-------------|---------------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| python      | 95% unit     | nightly + on-merge   | aria-patel         |
| javascript  | 90% unit     | nightly + on-merge   | samir-desai        |
| go          | 85% unit     | nightly              | lina-cho           |
| dotnet      | 80% unit     | weekly               | contract-maintain  |

Implementation patterns and helpers

- Validate with a lightweight contract library (recommended: internal package devx-contracts v0.x).
- Keep request/response fixtures in tests/fixtures/{unit,integration}, each under 200KB.
- Unit tests should use a local mock server (python: responses, node: nock, go: httptest).
- Integration tests run against the sandbox host: https://sandbox-api.redwood.company (token supplied via secrets).

Common failure modes and canonical fixes

1) Failure: Parsers crash when optional fields are missing
   - Symptom: KeyError/TypeError stack trace in the response deserializer.
   - Fix: Switch the parser to safe accessors with defaults, and add a unit test fixture that leaves the optional fields out.

2) Failure: Streaming tests hang in CI
   - Symptom: the GH Action job times out at 20m in the streaming scenario.
   - Fix: Have the test harness enforce a shorter read timeout (suggest 60s) and confirm the CI container has the right netcat/tcpreplay configs. Add a watchdog that cancels the read after N tokens.

3) Failure: Authentication flakes in integration runs
   - Symptom: intermittent 401s, mostly on long-running jobs.
   - Fix: Use short-lived test tokens refreshed at runtime, or the token rotation helper in ci/setup-env.sh. Log token expiry in telemetry.

4) Failure: Contract drift after a runtime change
   - Symptom: many SDK tests failing on mismatched field names.
   - Fix: Work with the runtime release owner to publish contract_delta.md. For urgent rollbacks, pin SDK CI to the previous contract via ci/contract_mocks.yaml.

Publisher checklist (pre-release)

- [ ] Update tests/contract.yaml if the API surface changed.
- [ ] Run the full integration suite locally against the sandbox.
- [ ] Bump the SDK version and add contract notes to the CHANGELOG.
- [ ] Tag the release and confirm CI publishes artifacts to the internal registry.

Troubleshooting commands and snippets

- Run unit contract tests locally:
  - Linux/macOS: ./ci/run_contract_unit_tests.sh --fast

- Replay a failing request against the sandbox:

```bash
# save the request body to request.json, then
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TEST_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://sandbox-api.redwood.company/v1/generate \
  --data-binary @request.json
```

- Build a diagnostic bundle for issues:

```bash
ci/collect_diagnostics.sh --output /tmp/sdk-diag.tar.gz
```

References and related pages

- API stability policy: /confluence/product-docs/requirements/api-stability-policy-2024
- Sandbox token request form: internal-service://devx/sandbox-keys
- DevEx CI templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/ci-templates-2025

Appendix: small checklist for SDK authors

- Keep fixtures small and clearly named.
- Note any contract.yaml change in plain language in the pull request description.
- Reproduce flaky network/time-sensitive tests in a clean container.
